extracted.intended_audience: observational astronomers / planetary observers and researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and criteria for long-term telescopic observation, recording, statistical analysis, and graphical representation ("cartouches") of visibility and seasonal change in Martian surface markings (canals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous, long and consecutive observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations must be numerous, consecutive, and extended in time (not merely occasional good observations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 372 drawings over six and a half months, 143 nights used, with portions of daily drawings for 46 consecutive days. The longer and more consecutive the record, the better the statistical elimination of accident or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate personal equation by single-observer data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible the same observer should make the drawings so that the personal equation of the observer—a very important source of deviation where drawings are to be compared—was eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes advantage of all drawings being made by one man; 'a man should be a machine in collecting his data, a mind in coördinating them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat each drawing as an independent, near-instantaneous datum
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing is as nearly an instantaneous picture of the disk as possible and thus counts as an independent determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings covered only a few minutes of observation and were made 'practically as if the observer had never seen the planet before.' In the study each canal had ~100 drawings yielding 10,900 separate determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct for extrinsic factors before inferring intrinsic change
rubrics_metrics.description: All factors outside the canal itself which could affect its visibility (distance, phase, seeing/definition, terrestrial and Martian atmosphere, position on disk) must be taken into account and corrected as nearly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position of central meridian was tabulated for each drawing; only drawings where the canal lay within 60° of centre were used (allowing for phase-side loss). Distance and seeing variations were considered and corrected for to isolate intrinsic visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record degree of strength as well as presence/absence
rubrics_metrics.description: Note not only the presence or absence of a marking but the degree of strength with which it is represented in each drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree-of-strength scoring was used in the final investigation; author remarks this made little difference to the final result but was nevertheless recorded to increase precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and use 'presentations' based on relative rotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize recurring intervals ('presentations') when a given region is well placed for observation owing to differing rotational periods; use presentations to compute visibility percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentations occur in 5–6 week cycles with about a fortnight for good central viewing. Visibility percentage at each presentation reflects intrinsic strength adjusted for definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute percentage visibility per canal from many eligible drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For each canal determine the percentage of eligible drawings (per presentation/period) in which it appears; these percentages track intrinsic changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 100 drawings were used per canal in the example; percentages after extrinsic corrections 'tell of the changes it has successively undergone and give us a history of its wax and wane.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot visibility percentages as 'cartouches' (time-series curves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot the successive true percentages of visibility vertically against time (days before/after a seasonal marker) and join points with a smooth curve—the canal's 'cartouche'—to reproduce continuous change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizontal axis: days from summer solstice (or other seasonal epoch); vertical axis: relative visibility. Cartouches graphically portray history, timing of minima/maxima, and relative strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret cartouche shapes as diagnostic of behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific curve shapes map to specific character of canal change (e.g., horizontal straight line = invariable; straight inclined = steady increase or decrease; various concave/convex curves indicate accelerating/decelerating changes, minima, maxima, inflection points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author provides an explicit mapping table of cartouche forms to interpretations (several curve patterns and their meanings). Use inflection points to locate times of minima/maxima and rate-of-change to infer acceleration or deceleration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cartouches to test reality vs illusion
rubrics_metrics.description: After correcting for extrinsic factors, cartouches that are curves or inclined lines are inconsistent with illusion theories; only horizontal straight-line cartouches could be produced by illusion or by invariable real phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion is presented as absolute: unless cartouches are approximately straight lines, illusion theories cannot explain the facts. Even then, straight lines could indicate either illusion or unchanging reality and require further assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate canals by latitude zones and compute mean cartouches
rubrics_metrics.description: Group canals into latitudinal belts (zones) and combine individual cartouches into mean cartouches for comparative, zonal analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example zones ~13° wide from 87°N down to ~27°S; mean cartouches reveal latitudinal progression of development (minima shifted progressively with latitude) and permit detection of planetary-scale waves of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate temporal behavior to planetary seasons and epoch markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor time-series to planetary seasonal markers (e.g., summer solstice, first frost, polar-cap melting) to interpret development timing and correlation with seasonal phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: tabulate days from summer solstice and vernal longitude; note dates (e.g., first frost) and compare with minima/maxima on cartouches to infer causal links (e.g., cold killing vegetation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select features for statistical inclusion based on sufficient frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Include in quantitative/statistical study only those canals/features that lend themselves by sufficient frequency of observation to a reliable statistical result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 109 canals chosen were the more conspicuous ones seen frequently enough to give about 100 determinations each; avoid including features too rarely seen to yield meaningful percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section long features and analyze parts separately
rubrics_metrics.description: For long canals, divide into contiguous sections and treat each section as if it were a separate canal to detect spatially varying development along the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Brontes divided into five sections (lengths in degrees given); 90 drawings used to produce section cartouches which revealed family resemblance but allowed finer-grained insight into development along the canal.
